resources.string: Turn your server into a node

Give the app your server\'s SSH login and it does the rest: installs the node, sets up its certificate, starts it, checks it, and adds it to your nodes. You don\'t need to know anything about servers.
A server running Ubuntu 20.04 or later, or Debian 11 or later, with at least 512 MB of memory; its address; and a user that is root or can use sudo, with its password or key.
Everything the server needs is inside this app. The server only downloads the operating system\'s own packages.
How do you log in to the server over SSH?
Enter the server\'s IP address or name.
Choose a private key file (OpenSSH or PEM).
Leave empty if the key has none.
The password or key is used only for this setup and is never saved. To update the node later, you enter it again.
How will contacts reach this node?
By its IP address (no domain needed)
Without a domain the node uses its own certificate, which the app pins. Contacts on app versions older than this one cannot reach you through it.
Point the domain\'s A (or AAAA) record at this server first. If a Let\'s Encrypt certificate can\'t be issued, the node still works with its own pinned certificate.
Blocks repeated SSH login attempts (fail2ban), installs security updates automatically, and keeps the clock in sync.
Turns password logins off. The app first checks that your key still gets in, and undoes it by itself if not.
Available when you log in with a key.
Keep your key file safe: after this, the server\'s password no longer lets anyone in over SSH, including you.
Your contacts reach you through this node. It is always added as a bootstrap node.
Checks the server and fixes common problems (package locks, broken mirrors, low memory)
Reachable by IP address, with a pinned certificate
Reachable at %1$s, with a Let\'s Encrypt certificate
Adds it to your nodes and uses it as your relay
Adds it to your nodes as a bootstrap node
This usually takes 3 to 10 minutes. Keep the app open.
Setting up your node. If the connection drops, the app picks up where it left off.
What was already done on the server stays; setting up again later continues from there.
The address carries the node\'s certificate pin, so share it as it is.
A Let\'s Encrypt certificate couldn\'t be issued, so the node uses its own pinned certificate. You can set it up again later to retry.
The node couldn\'t be added. Try again.
This is the server\'s fingerprint. If your provider shows one, check it matches. Nothing is sent to the server until you trust it.
This user needs its password to act as root.
That password was not accepted. Try again.
Check the node from this phone
The server reported a problem this version of the app doesn\'t know.
Something unexpected went wrong. Trying again usually helps.
The server didn\'t answer. Check the address and the SSH port, and that the server is on.
The server didn\'t accept this user with this password or key.
The key file couldn\'t be read. Check it\'s a private key and its passphrase is right.
The server\'s fingerprint has changed since you set it up. If you didn\'t reinstall it, someone may be in between. Nothing was sent.
The connection to the server was lost.
The sudo password was not accepted.
This user can\'t act as root. Log in as root, or as a user that can use sudo.
This server\'s system isn\'t supported. Use Ubuntu 20.04+ or Debian 11+ on x86-64 or ARM64.
This release hasn\'t been tested with the node. It will probably work.
This system release no longer gets security updates. Consider upgrading it.
The server has too little memory for a node (at least 512 MB is needed).
The server is low on disk space.
The server\'s clock is wrong. It will be corrected.
Apache is using the web ports. It will be stopped and disabled so the node can use them.
Another program uses port 443. The node will use a different port.
The server runs a newer node than this app carries. Continuing installs the older one.
A setup is already running on this server; the app joins it.
The domain doesn\'t point at this server yet, so the node uses its IP address.
A Let\'s Encrypt certificate couldn\'t be issued; the node uses its own pinned certificate.
The node runs, but this phone can\'t reach it. The provider\'s firewall may be blocking the port.
The node answered with a different certificate than the server reported. It was not added.
Key-only login was undone because the key couldn\'t log in with it. Password login still works.
Installing the system\'s packages failed. The server\'s package sources may be down.
A common problem on the server was fixed.
The node\'s ports were adjusted to fit what already runs on the server.
The web server\'s configuration has a problem; nothing of yours was changed.
The node didn\'t start correctly; the previous version was kept.
Part of securing the server didn\'t work; the node itself is fine.
The installer couldn\'t be sent to the server intact.
